The diple is a traditional woodwind from the Adriatic coast, an aerophone with reeds, Hornbostel–Sachs 422.12. Its construction is a single body containing two bores, so that it can sound two notes at once; it is played with the left hand on the left-hand holes and the right hand on the right-hand holes. The bagpipe diple has a double chanter and two single reeds, is fed from a goatskin bag, and plays melody and harmony together through the chanter; unlike most European bagpipes it has no drone. It is played traditionally in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Slovenia, Montenegro and Serbia.

A beginner can first practise steady blowing and the division of work between the hands, then learn to carry melody and harmony at once on the chanter. Regions differ in tuning, ornament and detail of handling, so a learner should adjust intonation and ornaments to the local tradition.
